newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 continues to slide as blue chips fall.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 continues to slide as blue chips fall.

text.p: Czech stocks continued their downward path on Monday as the Prague Stock Exchange's heaviest issues lost ground in quiet trading.

Telephone monopoly SPT Telecom lost 15 crowns to 3,400, and the country's largest commercial bank Komercni Banka fell 37 crowns to 1,680, pulling the PX50 index down 2.1 points, or 0.43 percent, to 489.0.
Overall on the PSE, 103 issues rose, while 84 fell and 66 held steady. A total of 490.876 shares changed hands on low turnover of 338.1 million crowns.
Dealer Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka said he expected quiet "summer activity" to arrive in the coming days with no large price swings.
Kusacek said he saw SPT shares stagnating or dipping as they had risen recently and some profit taking might take place. He said Komercni Banka could see some gains.
He added that Czech equities were interesting at current levels but some foreign investors were waiting for a further drop in the Czech crown.
"An up to five percent drop is generally expected. They also want to see the effect of government (restrictive) economic measures," he said.
The crown dropped about 10 percent of its value during May's speculative attack which forced the central bank to eliminate the currency's mark/dollar basket and let it float.
The currency crisis forced the government to adopt a package of austerity measures, including a total of 42 billion crowns in budget cuts.
The crown has recovered since, and it was trading about seven percent under its formal central parity on Monday afternoon.
